checks.quote: 422.520(a)(1): "the MA organization will pay 95 percent of the “clean claims” within 30 days of receipt if they are submitted by, or on behalf of, an enrollee of an MA private fee-for-service plan or are claims for services that are not furnished under a written agreement between the organization and the provider." (a)(3): "All other claims from non-contracted providers must be paid or denied within 60 calendar days from the date of the request." 422.504(c): "The MA organization must comply with the prompt payment provisions of § 422.520 and with instructions issued by CMS".
checks.correction: Confirmed as stated. Add the statute behind it: 42 U.S.C. 1395w-27(f)(1) requires the MA contract to provide "prompt payment (consistent with the provisions of sections 1395h(c)(2) and 1395u(c)(2) of this title) of claims ... if the services or supplies are not furnished under a contract between the organization and the provider or supplier". The 95 percent figure is a contract performance standard; per-claim interest under (a)(2) is owed on any clean claim paid after day 30. Guidance sec. 40.10 restates both clocks for non-contract providers and says for contract providers "The timeframe for processing payment requests is based on the contract terms".

checks.citation: 42 CFR 422.520(a)(2); 42 U.S.C. 1395u(c)(2)(C) and 1395h(c)(2)(C); Treasury Prompt Payment rate table; CMS Pub. 100-04 ch. 1 secs. 80.2.2 and 80.2.2.1

Treasury table: "Jul-26 through Dec-26 4.75%", "Jan-26 through Jun-26 4.125%", "Jul-25 through Dec-25 4.625%", "Jan-25 through Jun-25 4.625%". Pub. 100-04 80.2.2: "Payment amount x rate x days divided by 365 (366 in a leap year) = interest payment"; "The interest rate is determined by the applicable rate on the day of payment."
checks.correction: Rates, statute and regulation all confirmed. Two fixes for a cent-exact engine: (1) the FFS formula divides by 366 in a leap year, not always 365 (2028 is the next leap year); (2) sec. 80.2.2.1 says the contractor "applies interest to the net payment amount after all applicable deductions are determined (e.g., deductible, copayment, and/or MSP). Interest is rounded to the nearest penny." The exceptions the researcher flagged are confirmed in the FFS manual: interest is not paid on "Claims on which no payment is due" or "Full denials" (80.2.2), nor on "clean claims initially processed to denial and on which payment is made subsequent to the initial decision as a result of an appeal request" (80.2.2.1 C). No MA source applies or rejects those exceptions. The subparagraph mismatch is real in both 1395h(c)(2) and 1395u(c)(2): the interest sentence is (C).

checks.citation: CMS 'Provider Payment Dispute Resolution for Non-Contracted Providers' page (modified 09/10/2024); MMCM ch. 4 sec. 110.1.3 and ch. 6 sec. 100; MA Payment Guide for Out of Network Payments (4/15/2015) p. 12 'Physician Services'; 42 CFR 422.100(b)(1)-(2); 42 CFR 422.214(a)(1)
checks.quote: CMS page: "Medicare Advantage organizations, Cost plans, and PACE organizations are required to reimburse non-contract providers for Part A and Part B services provided to Medicare beneficiaries with an amount that is no less than the amount that would be paid under original Medicare." 422.100(b)(2): an MA plan "satisfies paragraph (a) of this section with respect to benefits for services furnished by a noncontracting provider if that MA plan provides payment in an amount the provider would have received under original Medicare (including balance billing permitted under Medicare Part A and Part B)." 422.214(a)(1): the non-contract provider "must accept, as payment in full, the amounts that the provider could collect if the beneficiary were enrolled in original Medicare." MMCM ch. 6 sec. 100: "In cases where the MA organization has not arranged for the services, if the non-contract provider's bill is less than the Original Medicare amount, the MA organization is only required to pay the billed amount."
checks.correction: The floor exists but its source must be stated accurately. The words "no less than" come from CMS guidance (the dispute page; MMCM ch. 4 sec. 110.1.3 says the plan "generally satisfies its requirements" by paying what the provider "would have been entitled to collect under original Medicare"). The regulations do not say it that way: 422.100(b)(2) is a safe harbor ("satisfies ... if"), and 422.214(a)(1) and statute 1852(k)(1) are a cap on what the provider may collect (MMCM ch. 6 sec. 100: "this provision of law imposes a cap on payment to non-contract providers"). Also the floor is the lesser of billed charges or the Original Medicare amount (OON guide: physicians "are paid using the lesser of billed charges, or the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS)"; non-par fee schedule "is 95% of the participating physician fee schedule"). Letters should cite the CMS page and MMCM, then 422.100(b)(2) and 422.214, and price each line at the lesser of the charge or the locality MPFS amount, net of the member's plan cost sharing.

422.510(a)(4): "(ii) Substantially failed to comply with the requirements in subpart M of this part relating to grievances and appeals. ... (v) Substantially failed to comply with the prompt payment requirements in § 422.520." 422.752(b): "If CMS makes a determination that could lead to a contract termination under § 422.510(a), CMS may impose the intermediate sanctions at § 422.750(a)(1) and (3)." 422.760(b)(1): "If the deficiency on which the determination is based has directly adversely affected (or has the substantial likelihood of adversely affecting) one or more MA enrollees—up to $25,000 as adjusted annually under 45 CFR part 102 for each determination." checks.correction: Grounds and remedies confirmed, three precisions: (1) for a 422.510(a) ground (appeals or prompt-pay failure) the intermediate sanctions available under 422.752(b) are suspension of enrollment and of communication activities only (422.750(a)(1) and (3)); suspension of payment for new enrollees (a)(2) is tied to the 422.752(a) list (e.g., (a)(1) substantial failure to provide medically necessary services that adversely affects enrollees). (2) The $25,000 per-determination and per-enrollee CMPs require a deficiency that "directly adversely affected (or has the substantial likelihood of adversely affecting)" enrollees; a pure provider-payment dispute with the member held harmless may not meet that test, while the per-week amount runs after CMS notice. (3) Current adjusted maximums in 45 CFR 102.3 (2025 column, the latest in eCFR as of 2026-11-19): $48,833 per determination (1395w-27(g)(3)(A)) and $19,535 per week (1395w-27(g)(3)(B)). These remain CMS's remedies, not the practice's.

The definition is a little wider than FIDE/HIDE with exclusively aligned enrollment: since January 1, 2023 it also covers a D-SNP whose enrollment, by State policy, is limited to members of an affiliated Medicaid managed care plan under a capitated contract (422.561, paragraph (2)(ii)). Which KY/IN plans qualify remains unconfirmed.

checks.citation: Humana 2026 Provider Manual (non-delegated) 'Provider Claims Dispute Process' and 'Medicare Appeals Process'; Humana 'Grievances and Appeals/Inquiry Directory' (954306ALL0226)
checks.quote: Manual: "Claims disputes must be received by Humana within 18 months from the date the provider received notice of the original claim determination unless state or federal law or the agreement requires another time period or the claim will not be reopened." "A nonparticipating provider can appeal claim denials for Medicare members only with a waiver of liability form for the following: • Full claim denials • Claims paying zero dollars • Claims denied for medical necessity • Claims denied for noncovered benefits". "Multiple provider dispute requests per provider encounter are generally unacceptable." Directory: "Please submit your appeal request in writing within 65 calendar days from the date of the denial notice." "Most inquiries receive a response in 30 to 45 days." "Humana Grievance and Appeal Department P.O. Box 14165 Lexington, KY 40512-4165".
checks.correction: Confirmed. One nuance: the 18-month dispute rule sits under "For all products: If providers disagree with Humana's initial adjudication of a claim, they may request a dispute", so it is not limited to contracted providers in the text; the email escalation (HumanaProviderServices@humana.com) is "Participating providers only" per the directory.

checks.citation: UnitedHealthcare 2026 Care Provider Administrative Guide ch. 10 'Claim reconsideration and appeals process', '20 or more claim reconsiderations (research request)' and 'Resolving potential reimbursement issues'; UHC 'Non-contracted care provider dispute and appeal rights' (PCA-1-24-03448-POE-QRG_01092025)
checks.quote: Admin Guide: "You must submit your reconsideration and appeal to us within 12 months from the date of the original claim EOB or PRA (or as required by law or your Agreement)." "If you have a request to reconsider 20 or more paid or denied claims for the same administrative issue (and attachments are not required), you may submit these in bulk online." "Unless your Agreement prescribes a different time frame, a Notice of Dispute must be sent no later than 60 days after the date of our decision on your appeal." "Failure to timely comply with this process and the requirements in your Agreement will result in the waiver of your right to initiate dispute resolution and waiver of your right to pursue such claim or issue in any forum." Non-contracted sheet: "You must file a dispute within 120 calendar days from the initial payment." "UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage has 30 calendar days to review and respond after receiving a payment dispute request." "you have 60 days from the denial date to file a payment reconsideration (appeal) request". "If the plan upholds all or part of the initial payment determination, we must forward the case to the CMS Independent Review Entity (IRE)".
checks.correction: Timelines confirmed. Two corrections: (1) the Claims Research Project is only for 20+ claims with "the same administrative issue (and attachments are not required)", so it does not carry medical-necessity or note-dependent reconsiderations; (2) missing the Notice of Dispute deadline waives more than arbitration: "waiver of your right to pursue such claim or issue in any forum". The non-contracted claim payment dispute is for cases where "you believe Original Medicare would have paid differently for the same service"; reconsiderations are for denials or when "we paid for a different service or level of service than what was billed".

checks.citation: Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Medicare Advantage Provider Guidebook, January 1, 2027 (Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield-CR-PM-017345-26-GRP4605, footer date November 1, 2026), secs. 5.3, 5.4, 6.1, 6.2, 7.1, 7.2
checks.quote: 5.3: "We accept reconsideration requests in writing, verbally and through our provider website within 120 calendar days from the date on the Explanation of Payment (EOP)"; "The plan will make every effort to resolve the claims payment reconsideration within 45 calendar days of receipt."; upheld letters include "Support for the action, including applicable statutes, regulations, policies, claims, codes, or provider manual references." 5.4: "within 30 calendar days of the date on the reconsideration determination letter"; "The plan will make every effort to resolve the claim payment appeal within 30 calendar days of receipt." 6.1: "Anthem typically determines provider appeals within 60 days when sufficient information is received"; 6.2: "Submitted within 180 days from the Anthem decision letter date." 7.2: "If a claim is partially or fully denied for payment with member liability (see original decision letter), the nonparticipating provider must request a reconsideration of the denial within 65 calendar days from the remittance notification. ... a signed Waiver of Liability Statement must be included."

checks.citation: Wellcare 2026 Medicare Advantage Provider Manual (4898664_NA6PCARCVRE, Internal Approved 04072026), Section 7 'Reimbursement / Non-Participating Provider Reimbursement', 'Reopening and Revising Determinations', 'Claims Payment Disputes'; Section 9 'Participating Provider Reconsiderations (Appeals)'
checks.quote: Sec. 9: "Providers have 90 calendar days from Wellcare's original utilization management review decision or claim denial to file a Provider appeal." "Upon receipt of all required documentation, Wellcare has up to 60 calendar days to review the appeal". Reimbursement: "All services rendered by non-participating Providers and facilities require authorization with the exception of family-planning education and counseling, in-office visits for family planning, childhood immunization administration, and emergency transportation and services. Non-participating Providers are reimbursed at 100% of the Medicare rate in effect on the date of service." Disputes: "Claim payment disputes received without the necessary documentation will be upheld by Wellcare due to lack of information." Reopening: "All decisions to grant reopening are at the discretion of Wellcare."
checks.correction: Quotes confirmed, but the provider_use needs two fixes: (1) the "100% of the Medicare rate" sentence follows a rule that all non-participating services "require authorization" except family planning, childhood immunization and emergency services, so a non-par letter citing the 100% floor must also show the authorization (or an exception); (2) the 90-day appeal and 60-day review are in Section 9 'Participating Provider Reconsiderations (Appeals)'; the manual says nothing about a Waiver of Liability for non-par appeals, so non-par Wellcare MA appeals fall back on CMS guidance 50.1.1 (WOL, 65 days). Also in Sec. 9: when an appeal is closed for lack of medical information, records must come "within 60 calendar days of the lack of medical information denial". Claims payment disputes: "Disputes should be filed within the applicable timeframe outlined in the Provider's contract and any state-specific requirements."

missing: Fax receipt starts the clock, even if misrouted. Parts C&D Appeals Guidance sec. 10.5.2 (https://www.cms.gov/medicare/appeals-and-grievances/mmcag/downloads/parts-c-and-d-enrollee-grievances-organization-coverage-determinations-and-appeals-guidance.pdf): requests are "received" when "A faxed document is successfully transmitted to the plan, as indicated on the fax transmission report", and "For standard requests, the processing timeframe begins when the plan, any unit in the plan, or a delegated entity (including a delegated entity that is not responsible for processing) receives a request." Sec. 10.5.1: "the day a plan receives the request is not counted as “day one.” “Day one” is the day after receipt of the request." Days "are calendar days unless otherwise specified and includes weekends and holidays". Use: keep every fax confirmation as the receipt proof for the 60-day reconsideration clock, and docket day 60 counting from the day after the confirmed transmission.

Plan-initiated reopenings and takebacks are time-limited. 42 CFR 422.616(a) applies Part 405 reopening rules ("may be reopened and revised by the entity that made the determination or decision, under the rules in part 405"); 42 CFR 405.980(b) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-11-19/title-42.xml?part=405&section=405.980): the deciding entity may reopen "(1) Within 1 year from the date of the initial determination ... for any reason. (2) Within 4 years ... for good cause as defined in § 405.986. (3) At any time if there exists reliable evidence ... that the initial determination was procured by fraud or similar fault". 405.986(a): good cause is "new and material evidence" or evidence that "clearly shows on its face that an obvious error was made". CMS FAQ Feb. 6, 2024 Q9 (https://www.cms.gov/files/document/hpms-memo-faq-coverage-criteria-and-utilization-management-020604pdf.pdf): post-claim reviews "must be compliant with reopening rules" and "If the revised determination is adverse, the notice to the parties must state the rationale and basis for the reopening and revision and any applicable right to appeal." Use: challenge MA recoupments older than 1 year that cite no new evidence, obvious error or fraud; applies with certainty to non-contracted claims, and to contracted claims at least through the FAQ.

Clerical errors must go through reopening, not appeal. Guidance sec. 80.4 (Part C): "An MA plan must remedy a clerical error (which include minor errors and omissions) using the reopening process instead of the appeal process"; clerical error includes "Mathematical or computational mistakes; Inaccurate data entry or coding; Computer errors; or Denials of claims as duplicates"; if the plan disagrees it "must dismiss the reopening request" and "must notify the party of their rights to appeal the initial adverse decision, provided timeframes to appeal the denial has not expired". Clerical-error reopenings can be requested "at any time" on an unfavorable determination (405.980(c)(3)). Cheapest route for sub-dollar unit, modifier and duplicate errors.

Plans must publish their prior authorization statistics. 42 CFR 422.122(c) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-11-19/title-42.xml?part=422&subpart=C): "Beginning in 2026, following each calendar year that it offers an MA plan, an MA organization must report prior authorization data ... at the MA contract level by March 31" and post "The percentage of standard prior authorization requests that were approved after appeal" and "The average and median time that elapsed between the submission of a request and a determination". Use: quote the plan's own posted overturn rate and decision times in PA disputes (Mohs, radiation).

Why Star Ratings are real money (the teeth behind C27, C30, C31). 42 CFR 422.258(d)(7)(i)(C) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-11-19/title-42.xml?part=422&subpart=F): a plan with "a quality rating of 4 stars or higher" gets its benchmark applicable percentage increased "For 2014 and subsequent years, by 5.0 percentage points" (doubled in qualifying counties, (d)(7)(ii)(B)); 422.266(a)(2)(ii): rebate share is "70 percent" at 4.5+ stars, "65 percent" at 3.5 to under 4.5, "50 percent" under 3.5; 422.260(b) defines quality bonus payments as "Enhanced CMS payments" and "Increased beneficiary rebate retention allowances". 42 CFR 422.510(a)(4)(xi) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-11-19/title-42.xml?part=422&subpart=K): CMS may terminate a contract that "Achieves a Part C summary plan rating of less than 3 stars for 3 consecutive contract years." Letters can state truthfully that late IRE forwards, IRE overturns and CTM complaints are inputs to the plan's Star Ratings, which set its bonus and rebates.

The plan answers for its vendors. 42 CFR 422.504(i)(1) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-11-19/title-42.xml?part=422&subpart=K): "Notwithstanding any relationship(s) that the MA organization may have with first tier, downstream, and related entities, the MA organization maintains ultimate responsibility for adhering to and otherwise fully complying with all terms and conditions of its contract with CMS." 42 CFR 422.562(a)(3) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-11-19/title-42.xml?part=422&subpart=M): if the plan delegates Subpart M duties, it "is ultimately responsible for ensuring that the entity or individual satisfies the relevant requirements of this subpart." Use: address appeals and complaints to the MA organization even when a claim-editing, payment-integrity or radiation-benefit vendor made the decision.

Contracted plans: notice duties, and the retaliation risk. 42 CFR 422.202(a)(1)-(2) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-11-19/title-42.xml?part=422&subpart=E): coordinated care plans must give physicians "Written notice of rules of participation including terms of payment" and "Written notice of material changes in participation rules before the changes are put into effect." Use: challenge a new edit or payment policy applied without prior written notice. Risk to weigh before aggressive letters: 422.202(d)(4): "An MA organization and a contracting provider must provide at least 60 days written notice to each other before terminating the contract without cause." The only anti-retaliation rules found protect physicians who request or support expedited determinations or reconsiderations (422.570(f), 422.584(f)); none protects a provider from contract termination for filing payment disputes.

How the ALJ amount in controversy is counted, and no ALJ deadline in Part C. 42 CFR 405.1006(d)(1) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-11-19/title-42.xml?part=405&section=405.1006): AIC is "the actual amount charged the individual for the items and services in the disputed claim, reduced by" payments made and collectable deductible/coinsurance; 405.1006(d)(6): when "the allowable amount has been paid in full and the appellant is challenging only the validity of the allowable amount", AIC is only the difference between the argued and published allowable. 405.1006(a)(2): "Delivery of similar or related services" means "like or coordinated services or items provided to one or more beneficiaries". Guidance sec. 70.4.1: "There are no statutory or regulatory decision-making timeframes for Part C appeals at the third level of review and beyond. See 42 CFR § 422.562(d)." 42 CFR 422.562(d)(2)(i)-(v) switch off the FFS adjudication deadlines and escalation options. Use: full denials reach $200 on billed charges quickly; pure rate underpayments need many lines; never promise an ALJ decision date.

New evidence is allowed later in MA appeals. 42 CFR 422.562(d)(2)(vi) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-11-19/title-42.xml?part=422&subpart=M): the Part 405 provisions "requiring a determination of good cause for the introduction of new evidence by a provider, supplier, or a beneficiary represented by a provider or supplier" do not apply under Subpart M; and 422.586: the plan "must provide the parties to the reconsideration with a reasonable opportunity to present evidence and allegations of fact or law, related to the issue in dispute, in person as well as in writing." Use: a missing note can still be added at the IRE or ALJ level for MA claims, unlike Original Medicare.

Records-missing denials and post-service authorization denials. Guidance sec. 40.12.1 'Notice on a Post-Service Authorization Request or Retrospective Review Decision' (https://www.cms.gov/medicare/appeals-and-grievances/mmcag/downloads/parts-c-and-d-enrollee-grievances-organization-coverage-determinations-and-appeals-guidance.pdf): such decisions are "subject to all applicable rules related to payment organization determinations"; "If an enrollee or provider request does not include sufficient information to process for payment, the plan must perform outreach for more information"; denied or dismissed payment requests require "the appropriate notice with appeal rights to the enrollee and provider"; plans "can develop payment policies that afford various flexibilities, such as waiver of any applicable prior authorization requirements." Sec. 10.6: "a minimum of one attempt to obtain additional information is sufficient", but "Plans are not required to conduct outreach prior to denying claims payments if they believe they have all the necessary information". Use: a denial for missing records with no outreach request is a procedural defect to cite.

Network gaps and plan-directed care (HMO non-par Mohs or pathology). MMCM ch. 4 sec. 110.1.3 (https://www.cms.gov/regulations-and-guidance/guidance/manuals/downloads/mc86c04.pdf): plans must "arrange for specialty care outside of the network, but at in-network cost-sharing" when "an enrollee requires a very specialized covered service that is not provided by the physicians in the network"; and "in the absence of a mutual agreement between the non-contracted provider and the MAO to receive less than the original Medicare rate, non-contracted providers must accept the original Medicare amount as payment in full." MMCM ch. 4 sec. 160 and 42 CFR 422.105(a): "CMS considers a contracted provider an agent of the MAO"; "If a contracted provider refers an enrollee to a non-contracted provider for a service that is covered by the plan upon referral, the enrollee is financially liable only for the applicable cost-sharing for that service." Use: answer 'out of network / no referral' denials of referred patients with the referral record and these sections.
